title: MiniFleet v0.3: quarantine flaky gates
summary: The fleet adds flaky-gate quarantine to itself, and the run is used to test the fleet's own repair loop with a deliberately injected defect.
intent: A gate that red-lights an unlucky run teaches people to ignore red, so the fleet needs to tell a flaky gate from a broken one. Add minifleet/quarantine.py: classify a series of gate outcomes as insufficient-data, stable-pass, stable-fail or flaky, and list the gates worth quarantining. Refuse to decide on a sample smaller than the minimum. Do this without breaking the engine, the shipped service, or the deployment path.
stakeholders: the on-call engineer who stops trusting red gates
deliverables: minifleet/quarantine.py - classify repeated gate outcomes and list flaky gates
the existing engine, service and deployment gates, still green
constraints: harness/ is frozen: workers may read it, never modify it
the engine's existing behaviour and the shipped linksvc service must be unaffected
out_of_scope: automatically re-running gates to collect samples

acceptance.statement: classify() labels all-pass as stable-pass, all-fail as stable-fail and mixed outcomes as flaky, with an exact pass_rate and sample count
A sample smaller than min_samples - including an empty one - is insufficient-data with a null pass_rate, never a verdict
Exactly min_samples outcomes are enough to decide; the boundary is inclusive
quarantine() returns only flaky gates, sorted, and never quarantines insufficient data
The pre-existing engine regression suite still passes on the integrated tree
The shipped linksvc service still passes its own acceptance harness
The fleet can still deploy a running system and probe it: ready under 10s, p50 under 50ms

engine regression on the integrated tree
shipped service still passes its own harness
deploy and observe the shipped service
the new module is where the contract says

exports.minifleet.quarantine.classify: classify(outcomes: list[bool], min_samples: int = 3, flake_threshold: float = 0.5) -> {'verdict': str, 'pass_rate': float|None, 'samples': int, 'dominant': str|None}
exports.minifleet.quarantine.quarantine: quarantine(gates: dict[str, list[bool]], min_samples: int = 3, flake_threshold: float = 0.5) -> list[str]

contracts.content:
## Exact semantics

`classify(outcomes, min_samples=3, flake_threshold=0.5)`:

- `len(outcomes) < min_samples` -> verdict `insufficient-data`, `pass_rate` **None**, `samples` = len, `dominant` None. An empty list is the `samples: 0` case of this rule.
- otherwise `pass_rate = round(passes / samples, 3)` and verdict is all of: `stable-pass` when the rate is 1.0, `stable-fail` when it is 0.0, otherwise `flaky`.
- `dominant` is `pass` when `pass_rate >= flake_threshold` else `fail`; for a stable verdict it matches the verdict; for `insufficient-data` it is None.
- `min_samples` <= 0 raises ValueError. A non-boolean entry raises TypeError.

`quarantine(gates, min_samples=3, flake_threshold=0.5)` returns the gate ids whose verdict is exactly `flaky`, sorted ascending. Gates with insufficient data are never returned.
